routes.name: architect
routes.description: System design, trade-offs, migrations and technology choices grounded in the codebase
routes.when_to_use: Use when a change crosses boundaries, is hard to reverse, or needs a design first.

routes.name: builder
routes.description: Implements a scoped feature or fix test-first with the smallest passing change, verified by the project's checks
routes.when_to_use: Use when the design is settled and code needs writing.

routes.name: ccc
routes.description: Commander's click-first home: reads the project context, then routes to build, review, ship or the More menu (plan, x-ray, Codex CLI, fleet, connectors, plugin audit workflows) in one or two clicks
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user types /ccc, opens the Commander menu, or asks where to start.

routes.name: ccc-adhd
routes.description: Answer-first output: the fix, then command, then file:line, context last. Toggle on, off or status; stacks with caveman. Based on ayghri/i-have-adhd (MIT)
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user wants the answer first.

routes.name: ccc-adopt
routes.description: Merge Commander's orchestrator/executor section and a stack-tailored skill and agent list into an existing project's CLAUDE.md as a delimited, re-runnable block, with backup and diff approval first
routes.when_to_use: Use when adopting Commander conventions in a repo you already have.

routes.name: ccc-agent-writing
routes.description: Draft a spec, PRD, PR description, README section, runbook or technical doc that a reader can act on without a follow-up question: named reader, answer first, typed structure, self-test
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user says write a spec, draft a PRD, write the PR description, or document this.

routes.name: ccc-brainstorm
routes.description: Design-first ideation gate: three parallel agents propose a simple, a scalable and a user-delight approach, rendered as a tradeoff matrix, then you pick a direction. No code is written
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks how to build X, which approach to take, is torn between options, or types /ccc-brainstorm.

routes.name: ccc-broadcast
routes.description: Relay build, deploy, CI, task and cost outcomes as short scrubbed summaries to a connected team chat or email, so non-developers see what shipped
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user wants the team, owner or a client told when a deploy, build or run finishes, or types /ccc-broadcast.

routes.name: ccc-browse
routes.description: Browse every CC Commander skill, agent and domain: publish the searchable Cockpit catalog page after consent, or drill in four at a time with pickers and launch one
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks what Commander can do, wants the catalog, or types /ccc-browse.

routes.name: ccc-build
routes.description: Scaffold a new web app, API or CLI from a three-question spec interview, built by a background agent and verified before it is called ready
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user wants to build something new, start a project, create an app, or types /ccc-build.

routes.name: ccc-changelog
routes.description: Summarize what changed in the latest CC Commander release, or a named version, from CHANGELOG.md in a short scan-friendly digest
routes.when_to_use: Use when asking what's new, what changed, show the changelog, release notes, or after the SessionStart update nudge.

routes.name: ccc-cheatsheet
routes.description: Live map of Commander: reads the installed plugin's skills, workflows, menus, agents, hooks and MCP servers from disk and renders a Mermaid flow plus a navigator picker, with an optional HTML export
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user types /ccc-cheatsheet or asks for a command map or everything Commander offers.

routes.name: ccc-ci
routes.description: Diagnose CI and deploy failures: pull the failing run's log, classify the cause, propose a fix, and follow runs with /loop or a Routine; optional signed-webhook push mode
routes.when_to_use: Use when CI is red, a deploy failed, a prod approval waits, or the user wants pipeline events in the session.

routes.name: ccc-claudemd
routes.description: Audit a project CLAUDE.md against the real codebase for stale paths, dead commands, missing context and token waste, then apply fixes only after picker approval
routes.when_to_use: Use when asking to audit, clean up or optimize CLAUDE.md or project instructions, or when the suggest engine flags it as stale.

routes.name: ccc-code-review
routes.description: Alias for /ccc-review: forwards a code, PR or diff review request with its arguments to the canonical review workflow
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user types /ccc-code-review or asks to review code, a PR, a file or a diff by this name.

routes.name: ccc-codex
routes.description: Manage the OpenAI Codex CLI: doctor, models, plugins, MCP servers, custom agents, cloud tasks, remote control, reviews, updates, import and config, backing up config first
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks to check, set up or manage Codex.

routes.name: ccc-connect
routes.description: Opt-in connector wizard with affiliate disclosure: pick a service (Supabase, Linear, Vercel, Sentry, Notion, Slack, Stripe, research tools and more) and wire it as a plugin with userConfig, an OAuth MCP or a keyed MCP without secrets in chat
routes.when_to_use: Use when connecting an MCP server or service.

routes.name: ccc-console
routes.description: Open the Commander Console inline (agents, usage, safety, memory, history, launch chips, prompt bar) or publish one tab as a private snapshot page after consent
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks what is going on, wants the console, or types /ccc-console.

routes.name: ccc-content
routes.description: Draft blog posts, social threads, email campaigns, landing-page copy and docs in three questions, with an optional brief, review and scheduling pipeline
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks to write a post, thread, newsletter, email campaign or marketing copy, repurpose a URL, or types /ccc-content.

routes.name: ccc-data
routes.description: Route data work to the right method: ETL/ELT pipelines, SQL optimization, charts and dashboards, machine learning, data quality, product analytics, scheduled reports, or vector search
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user is building, querying, validating or visualizing data, or types /ccc-data.

routes.name: ccc-debate
routes.description: Adversarial multi-agent debate: lens agents (security, performance, architecture, product, contrarian) argue and cross-examine one design, plan or diff, then a judge rules ship, revise or block
routes.when_to_use: Use when a decision is costly to reverse, a diff touches auth or billing, or the user types /ccc-debate.

routes.name: ccc-deploy
routes.description: Deploy the current build to Vercel, Fly.io, Cloudflare, GitHub Pages, npm, or a package deploy script, verify the live URL, and draft post-deploy notes
routes.when_to_use: Use when a build is ready to go live or the user says deploy, push to production, or publish the package.
triggers: build is ready to go live

routes.name: ccc-deploy-check
routes.description: Pre-deploy readiness gate: tests, build, debug logs, secrets, TODOs, lockfile and destructive-migration checks with a GO, CAUTION or NO-GO verdict, plus risk and rollback plan in power mode
routes.when_to_use: Use when asking ready to ship, should I deploy, is it safe, deploy check, or pre-deploy.

routes.name: ccc-design
routes.description: Route design work to the right method: landing page, component system, Impeccable polish pass, Figma to code, chat UI, Design.md capture or screenshot to interactive UI
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user wants to design, restyle, polish or animate a UI, or types /ccc-design.

routes.name: ccc-devops
routes.description: DevOps domain router: picks the right specialist for CI/CD pipelines, zero-downtime deploys, Docker and container security, AWS, Terraform, Prometheus/Grafana monitoring, networking and runbooks, then loads it
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user wants to set up, harden or plan infrastructure or delivery.

routes.name: ccc-doc-sync
routes.description: Sync skill, agent and hook-handler counts and the version string across Commander docs from contract.json and package.json, with a --check drift gate for CI
routes.when_to_use: Use when counts or the version changed, after adding a skill, agent or handler, or when a doc-count check fails.

routes.name: ccc-doctor
routes.description: Paste-ready Commander health report: install mode, installed vs latest version, clone and cache state, settings, MCP servers, plugin validate and details, mods, Codex doctor, optional source drift checks
routes.when_to_use: Use when Commander misbehaves, after an update, or before filing a support issue.

routes.name: ccc-domains
routes.description: Alias for /ccc-learn: opens the domain picker to browse and load a skill domain such as design, marketing, SaaS, testing, DevOps or security
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user types /ccc-domains, says 'domain skills' or 'show categories', or asks which skills exist for a field.

routes.name: ccc-e2e
routes.description: Pre-release assessment that fans out via /ccc-fleet into up to three isolated workers (QA audit, unit tests, Playwright E2E) running /ccc-testing lanes, then writes a severity-ranked PASS or FAIL verdict
routes.when_to_use: Use when about to tag a release, after a large merge, or asking is this ready.

routes.name: ccc-ecc
routes.description: Selective ECC loader: pick one Everything Claude Code skill, agent or hook from the vendored checkout and symlink or copy only that component into ~/.claude, with a backup, never the full harness
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user wants a single ECC component without installing ECC.
triggers: single ecc component without installing ecc

routes.name: ccc-fable
routes.description: Arm, check, audit or disarm the Fable Method: the PM loop, 12 checkable gates, workflow-first posture and verifier separation, persisted in Commander state
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user says fable on/off/status/audit or wants verification-gated, orchestrated work.

routes.name: ccc-fleet
routes.description: Run parallel agents on one task: fan-out slices in isolated worktrees, a sequential pipeline, a review panel, a background run, or a director-lead-specialist team, then verify and synthesize
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user types /ccc-fleet or wants work split across several agents.
triggers: wants work split across several agents

routes.name: ccc-fleet-viz
routes.description: Show a /ccc-fleet run as a live tree of workers (done, running, failed, waiting) with branches and a Mermaid diagram, refreshing until every worker finishes
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for fleet progress, types /ccc-fleet-viz, or a /ccc-fleet run completes.

routes.name: ccc-handoff
routes.description: Write a dense handoff file and tell the user to resume in a new chat before a long context degrades output quality
routes.when_to_use: Use when a chunk of work is done, the topic is about to switch, the model starts forgetting context, or a long orchestration run is mid-flight.

routes.name: ccc-harden
routes.description: Pre-launch production hardening audit across hosting, GitHub, error tracking, analytics, payments, secrets/PII headers and Cloudflare. Read-only by default; per-pillar fixes only with approval. Findings stay local
routes.when_to_use: Use when preparing a launch or security review, or after config changes.

routes.name: ccc-hermes
routes.description: Optional bridge between Claude Code and a local Hermes agent gateway: chat channels can wake a Claude Code session, and Claude Code can post progress or accept escalations over MCP
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user runs a Hermes gateway and wants channel triggers, progress posts or hand-offs.

routes.name: ccc-infra
routes.description: Dev services status: probes the local services you declare in an optional services.json, plus Claude MCP connections and Codex CLI health, and recommends the next action
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for infrastructure or service status, whether a dev server is up, or why an MCP is down.
triggers: whether a dev server is up

routes.name: ccc-knowledge
routes.description: Search, browse and add lessons in the local CC Commander knowledge base: recent lessons, topic search, category view, stats and file-edit captures
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks what we learned, wants past lessons, the knowledge base, or types /ccc-knowledge.

routes.name: ccc-learn
routes.description: Pick a CC Commander skill domain in one click (design, marketing, SaaS, DevOps, SEO, testing, security, data and more) and hand off to that domain's router skill
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks what skills exist, wants the skill catalog, says learn or browse domains, or types /ccc-learn.

routes.name: ccc-linear
routes.description: View your open Linear issues, pick one to work on (moves it to In Progress and creates a branch), create a new issue, or see a board overview, all from pickers
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user types /ccc-linear, asks for their Linear issues or tickets, or wants to start work from a ticket.

routes.name: ccc-linear-board
routes.description: Publish a team's Linear issues as a private Kanban page whose cards update in place from a shared data store, or hand off to /ccc-linear to view, pick or create issues in chat
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for a Linear board page, a sprint board to share, or types /ccc-linear-board.

routes.name: ccc-loop
routes.description: Pick the right loop primitive (turn, /goal, /loop interval or self-paced, ScheduleWakeup, Routines via /schedule), gate it, give it an independent verifier and a state file
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user wants recurring, polling, run-until-done or unattended agent work.

routes.name: ccc-makeover
routes.description: Score project health with /ccc-xray, apply the top recommendations one at a time with your OK, and show a before/after report card
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for a health check, wants the top issues fixed automatically, asks for a project score or report card, or types /ccc-makeover.
triggers: wants the top issues fixed automatically

routes.name: ccc-marketing
routes.description: Route marketing work to the right specialist method: brand context, content, conversion optimization, email and ads, growth experiments, competitor intelligence, pricing and launches
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for marketing help, CRO, a campaign or launch plan, or types /ccc-marketing.

routes.name: ccc-memory
routes.description: Keep durable project memory in two tiers: CLAUDE.md for always-loaded facts and a memory/ directory of dated notes, decisions, gotchas and preferences loaded on demand
routes.when_to_use: Use when recording a decision, root cause, correction or preference future sessions must keep.

routes.name: ccc-mission-control
routes.description: Agent mission control: who is working on what, as a local live dashboard, a plain-English status, suggestion triage, or a private snapshot page whose task board updates in place
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks what agents are doing, wants a status board, or types /ccc-mission-control.

routes.name: ccc-mobile
routes.description: Route mobile work to the right method: React Native/Expo, Flutter, SwiftUI or Jetpack Compose builds, mobile testing, app store optimization, push notifications and deep links, or start a new app
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user is building, testing or shipping an iOS or Android app, or types /ccc-mobile.

routes.name: ccc-more
routes.description: Commander's second-page menu: plan, x-ray, Codex CLI management, fleet, Linear, connectors, tune-up, catalog browse and the plugin audit workflows, one click each
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user picks More tools in /ccc, types /ccc-more, or asks what else Commander can do.
triggers: asks what else commander can do

routes.name: ccc-night-mode
routes.description: Spec-first autonomous build that runs overnight or immediately in multi-cycle build and independent-review loops, checkpointing status each cycle and stopping at a budget
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user says night mode, yolo mode, overnight build, or build while I sleep.

routes.name: ccc-nightwatch
routes.description: Remote permission relay for unattended runs: risk-classify each tool call, auto-allow reads, send risky calls to your phone via Telegram or Discord for a tap, hard-deny destructive ones
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user wants to approve from phone, remote YOLO, or run overnight with a safety leash.
triggers: run overnight with a safety leash

routes.name: ccc-onboard
routes.description: Contributor first-hour plan for the current repository: reads CLAUDE.md, BIBLE.md and package.json, checks required tools, asks the contributor's role, and returns a five-step checklist plus five real starter resources
routes.when_to_use: Use when someone new joins a repo or types /ccc-onboard.

routes.name: ccc-orchestrate
routes.description: Write a goal file, run it on a separate executor (Codex GPT-6 or a Sonnet subagent) in an isolated worktree, then verify every acceptance criterion
routes.when_to_use: Use when a task benefits from a different executor and independent verification.

routes.name: ccc-plan
routes.description: Turn an idea, bug, refactor or Linear issue into a reviewed plan file with evals, via a short spec interview and a background planner agent that writes to the session plan path
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user wants to plan a feature, scope work before coding, or types /ccc-plan.

routes.name: ccc-plan-exec
routes.description: Plan cheap, execute capable: a fast model drafts the loop (steps, per-step body, verify condition), a capable model runs each step in an isolated worktree with an independent verifier
routes.when_to_use: Use when work repeats one body over many items, or the user says plan-exec, write a loop, or types /ccc-plan-exec.

routes.name: ccc-prompt-fix
routes.description: Diagnose a prompt against the six prompt-quality patterns and return a tighter rewrite with the reason for each change, a 0-6 score, or the best matching prompt from the Commander prompt library
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks to fix, sharpen, improve or score a prompt, or wants a prompt for a task.
triggers: wants a prompt for a task

routes.name: ccc-qa
routes.description: QA pass before shipping: detects the framework, runs unit, integration and E2E suites, computes the coverage delta, audits flaky tests and has qa-engineer severity-rate gaps
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for a QA pass, to run all tests, check coverage, find flaky tests or if it is ready to ship.
triggers: if it is ready to ship

routes.name: ccc-recall
routes.description: Search past saved sessions and curated memory notes for an earlier fix, decision or file, and answer with the source file and date cited
routes.when_to_use: Use when asking didn't we solve this before, what did we decide about X, or when a bug first appeared.
triggers: asking didn't we solve this before
what did we decide about x

routes.name: ccc-relay
routes.description: Chain independent loop sessions (spec, build, review, then a human-gated merge) that hand off through a durable state file, tracker status or reaction, each link separately gated and verified
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user types /ccc-relay, wants the Finn Loop, or wants auto-chained loops.

routes.name: ccc-research
routes.description: Research before you build: cited multi-source research, spec interviews, cross-model review, literature reviews, competitive and trend analysis, and large-document or large-codebase ingestion
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user wants options compared, prior art found, a spec defined, or something too big summarized.

routes.name: ccc-resume-session
routes.description: Load a saved session file from ~/.claude/sessions/ (latest, by date, or by path), read it fully, and brief project, state, what not to retry, blockers and next step before touching anything
routes.when_to_use: Use when resuming work, continuing where you left off, or after a fresh session.

routes.name: ccc-review
routes.description: Audit the current branch, security posture, performance hot paths or the whole project; routes to /commander:ccc-deep-review, built-in /code-review or a specialist agent and writes a severity-rated report to tasks/reviews/
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for a code review, PR review, audit or /ccc-review.

routes.name: ccc-rollback
routes.description: Roll production back by picking a known-good commit or tag, creating atomic git revert commits, pushing them, redeploying through the /ccc-deploy runners, and verifying health
routes.when_to_use: Use when a deploy is bad, production is broken, or the user asks to revert or roll back a release.

routes.name: ccc-saas
routes.description: Route SaaS work to the right method: scaffold, auth, database, API, frontend, Stripe billing, webhooks, multi-tenancy, feature flags, metrics and conversion
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user is building, billing or growing a SaaS product, or types /ccc-saas.

routes.name: ccc-safety
routes.description: Safety deck: dangerous actions Commander's hooks blocked, auto-fixes applied, and the tools that fail most, narrated here or published as a private snapshot page after consent
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks what the guardrails caught, why tools fail, or types /ccc-safety.

routes.name: ccc-save-session
routes.description: Compress the current session into a dense reloadable file in ~/.claude/sessions/: decisions, files touched, what worked, what failed and why, open questions, exact next step
routes.when_to_use: Use when ending a session, nearing context limits, or saying save this session.

routes.name: ccc-security
routes.description: Application security hub: built-in /security-review plus lanes for OWASP Top 10, secrets, dependency CVEs, prompt-injection defense, CodeQL CI, variant analysis and incident response
routes.when_to_use: Use when asked to audit security, scan for secrets or vulnerable packages, harden an AI app, or handle a breach.

routes.name: ccc-seo
routes.description: Route SEO work to the right method: technical audit and fixes, AI search optimization (AEO, GEO, LLMO), content clusters and briefs, analytics, programmatic pages, backlinks and social previews
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks to audit or improve SEO, rank in AI answers, plan SEO content, or types /ccc-seo.

routes.name: ccc-session
routes.description: Alias that routes session work to the canonical skills: save the current session with /ccc-save-session, or reload a saved one with /ccc-resume-session
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user says resume session, continue where I left off, save this session, or types /ccc-session.

routes.name: ccc-settings
routes.description: Settings hub: Commander preferences (name, level, cost ceiling, theme, animations, launch mode, Linear, reset) plus Claude Code permission mode, effort, model restrictions and workflow size, each written with a backup
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user says settings, configure, change theme, set effort, auto mode.

routes.name: ccc-ship
routes.description: Ship menu: run a parallel pre-flight matrix with a GO, CAUTION or NO-GO scorecard, cut a tagged release with changelog, deploy to a platform, or roll back the last deploy, each gated by a picker
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user says ship it, pre-flight, cut a release, tag a version, or roll back.

routes.name: ccc-smb-ops
routes.description: Small-business back office from a bank CSV or a typed list: 13-week cash-flow forecast, invoicing and AR chasing, payroll planning, CRM cleanup, expense tracking, and a Monday owner brief
routes.when_to_use: Use when an owner asks about cash, unpaid invoices, payroll, contacts, spending, or the weekly picture.

routes.name: ccc-spawn
routes.description: Spin self-contained work off on demand: a background subagent, a separate session (Cowork spawn_task chip or CLI /spawn peer), or an independent expert pass; routes fan-outs to /ccc-fleet and chains to /ccc-relay
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user types /ccc-spawn or wants a task done outside this thread.

routes.name: ccc-standup
routes.description: Write a yesterday / today / blockers standup from your commits, PRs, tracker issues and Commander session notes, or from rough notes you type
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for a standup, daily update, morning check-in, what did I do yesterday, or a team update.

routes.name: ccc-start
routes.description: First-run Commander onboarding: detects the setup live, offers new-project, import, tour or skip pickers, writes a start plan file and marks onboarding complete
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user just installed Commander, types /ccc-start, or asks how to get started.

routes.name: ccc-suggest
routes.description: Reads project state and recent activity, then recommends one next /ccc-* workflow, skill or plugin with named reasons and picker alternatives; also runs as a standing PM loop
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks what next, which tool to use, or is stuck.

routes.name: ccc-systematic-debugging
routes.description: Root-cause debugging under one law: no fix without a confirmed root cause. Reproduce, compare, hypothesize, then fix once with a failing test first
routes.when_to_use: Use when investigating a bug, a failing or flaky test, or an error of unknown cause.

routes.name: ccc-tasks
routes.description: Track work in one markdown file, tasks/todo.md, with checkboxes, P0-P3 priorities and status marks; no database, service or sync
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks for a todo list, wants to track personal or side-session tasks, or types /ccc-tasks.

routes.name: ccc-testing
routes.description: Testing domain router: picks the lane for TDD, E2E, visual regression, load testing, QA, regression checks, evals or verification and runs test-writing work in an isolated worktree
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks to write tests, plan a test strategy, or test, verify or load-test a change.

routes.name: ccc-triage
routes.description: Triage a GitHub repo's open issues and PRs with the gh CLI: flag stale, unlabeled and CI-failing items, propose labels and next actions, apply labels one confirmed item at a time, or summarize the backlog
routes.when_to_use: Use when a maintainer asks to triage issues or PRs, label the backlog, or wants a digest.

routes.name: ccc-tuneup
routes.description: Audit and safely optimize the local Commander setup: version freshness, junk, count drift, superseded agents, hooks, settings keys, MCP staleness and cost settings. Read-only scan first; backs up, archives (never deletes) and asks before any fix
routes.when_to_use: Use when the setup feels cluttered, stale or slow.

routes.name: ccc-ultracode
routes.description: Run deep, multi-agent work as adversarially verified workflows: repo audits, branch reviews, migrations, fleets. Explains the /effort ultracode toggle and launches the bundled Commander workflows
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user types /ccc-ultracode or wants depth over speed on repo-wide work.

routes.name: ccc-update
routes.description: Update the installed CC Commander plugin: detect the install mode and installed vs latest version, hand over the exact update commands, then verify the installed runtime and hooks after restart
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks to update Commander or suspects an outdated install.

routes.name: ccc-upgrade
routes.description: Maintainer-only vendor submodule updater: audits every submodule under vendor/ against upstream, shows commits and files behind, then updates the picked ones one at a time with audit checks and one commit each
routes.when_to_use: Use when asked to update vendors, refresh submodules or check vendor drift.

routes.name: ccc-usage
routes.description: Usage and cost deck: estimated savings from routing to cheaper models, cost per day and cost by app, narrated here or published as a private snapshot page after consent
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user asks what agent work costs, how much was saved, or types /ccc-usage.

routes.name: ccc-xray
routes.description: Project health scorecard: scans the current repo for quality, docs, tests, deps, security, performance, CI, session cost and plugin context cost, then returns 0-100 scores with one fix-first call
routes.when_to_use: Use when asked for a health check, repo audit, x-ray or token-cost inventory.

routes.name: ccc-yolo-setup
routes.description: Cut approval prompts safely: keep auto permission mode, add a vetted read-only allowlist plus secret deny rules, back up settings, and set bypassPermissions only with explicit consent
routes.when_to_use: Use when the user says yolo setup, reduce prompts, fewer approvals, or skip permissions.

routes.name: content-strategist
routes.description: Content strategy and draft copy for a named reader: plans, posts, landing pages, emails, social. Drafts only
routes.when_to_use: Use to plan, draft, edit or audit content.

routes.name: csharp-reviewer
routes.description: Read-only C#/.NET review: async/await, IDisposable, LINQ, nullable types, DI lifetimes, security
routes.when_to_use: Use when a diff touches .cs or .csproj files.

routes.name: data-analyst
routes.description: Read-only data analysis with sample sizes, confidence, chart specs and reproducible queries
routes.when_to_use: Use when a question needs an answer from data or a metric moved.
triggers: question needs an answer from data

routes.name: debugger
routes.description: Root-cause debugging: reproduce, confirm the cause with evidence, apply a minimal fix and prove it with a regression test. Use for bugs, flaky tests or errors of unknown cause

routes.name: designer
routes.description: UI/UX design and frontend implementation on the existing design system, WCAG AA, checked across widths
routes.when_to_use: Use to build, polish or critique an interface.

routes.name: devops-engineer
routes.description: CI/CD, containers, IaC, deploys and monitoring, each with a preview and rollback plan
routes.when_to_use: Use to set up or fix CI, write Dockerfiles or Terraform, or plan a deploy.

routes.name: fleet-worker
routes.description: Parallel worker for one scoped fleet task: stays in its files, runs the named checks, returns a structured report
routes.when_to_use: Use when /ccc-fleet or an orchestrator fans out work.

routes.name: go-reviewer
routes.description: Read-only Go review: goroutine and channel safety, errors, context propagation, idioms, security
routes.when_to_use: Use when a diff touches .go code or go.mod.

routes.name: java-reviewer
routes.description: Read-only Java review: null safety, resources, Spring pitfalls, concurrency, security
routes.when_to_use: Use when a diff touches .java code, pom.xml or build.gradle.

routes.name: kotlin-reviewer
routes.description: Read-only Kotlin review: null safety, coroutines, idioms, Android lifecycle and security
routes.when_to_use: Use when a diff touches .kt or .kts code.

routes.name: performance-engineer
routes.description: Read-only performance audit: hot paths, measured or estimated cost, and fixes ranked by impact and effort
routes.when_to_use: Use when something is slow or a budget regressed.

routes.name: product-manager
routes.description: Feature scoping, PRDs, user stories with testable acceptance criteria, metrics and prioritization
routes.when_to_use: Use to turn an idea into a buildable spec or to order a backlog.

routes.name: python-reviewer
routes.description: Read-only Python review: type hints, async, idioms, pytest quality and security. Returns path:line findings
routes.when_to_use: Use when a diff touches .py code or packaging.

routes.name: qa-engineer
routes.description: Adversarial QA in an isolated worktree: breaking-case tests, coverage delta and reproducible bug reports
routes.when_to_use: Use to test a feature, close coverage gaps or verify a fix.

routes.name: researcher
routes.description: Sourced research with dated citations and observed/inferred/speculative labels, ending in recommendations
routes.when_to_use: Use when a decision depends on facts not yet in hand.

routes.name: reviewer
routes.description: Read-only review of a diff or PR for correctness, security, performance and maintainability. Returns path:line findings and a verdict
routes.when_to_use: Use before merging a change.

routes.name: rust-reviewer
routes.description: Read-only Rust review: ownership, unsafe soundness, async/Tokio, error handling, clippy idioms, security
routes.when_to_use: Use when a diff touches .rs code or Cargo.toml.

routes.name: security-auditor
routes.description: Read-only security audit: OWASP/CWE-mapped findings with exploit path, fix and verification
routes.when_to_use: Use when code touches untrusted input, auth, secrets or dependencies.

routes.name: technical-writer
routes.description: Developer docs written from the code: READMEs, API references, guides, architecture overviews, changelogs
routes.when_to_use: Use when docs are missing, stale or hard to follow.

routes.name: typescript-reviewer
routes.description: Read-only TypeScript/JavaScript review: type safety, async, ESM/CJS, runtime boundaries, security
routes.when_to_use: Use when a diff touches .ts, .tsx, .js or .mjs code.
